Title: Determination of the Kinetic Parameters for the Crystallization of Paracetamol from Water Using Metastable Zone Width Experiments

Abstract: A new approach for the estimation of kinetic parameters of crystallization from data obtained during the determination of metastable zone width is presented. The method is based on a simplified dynamic model of the system, which combines the population balance and mass balance, as well as information provided by concentration and particle size distribution measurements using ATR-FTIR spectroscopy and laser backscattering to determine simultaneously the nucleation and growth parameters from the experimental data. The application of the proposed approach is illustrated for the cooling crystallization of paracetamol from water. The technique is compared to existing approaches for the determination of nucleation parameters from metastable zone width experiments and is used to corroborate the assumptions used in the classical approaches. The key conclusion is that the assumptions made in the existing approaches, which simplifies the parameters' estimation procedure, can result in substantial error in the nucleation kinetics.

Model: Dynamic crystallization moment model
Laws:
(11.1) [balance] The zeroth moment of the crystal size distribution increases at the primary nucleation rate.
(11.2) [balance] The first moment of the crystal size distribution changes through crystal growth and the birth of crystals at size r0.
(11.3) [balance] The second moment of the crystal size distribution changes through growth and nucleation at size r0.
(11.4) [balance] The third moment of the crystal size distribution changes through growth and nucleation at size r0.
(11.5) [balance] The solution concentration decreases according to the rate at which crystal mass accumulates.
(12) [constitutive] The crystal growth rate follows a power law in the concentration difference.
(13) [constitutive] The primary number nucleation rate follows a power law in the concentration difference.
(21) [constitutive] The equilibrium concentration of paracetamol in water is correlated with temperature.

States (computed by the ODEs):
- \mu_{0}: Zeroth moment of the crystal size distribution.
- \mu_{1}: First moment of the crystal size distribution.
- \mu_{2}: Second moment of the crystal size distribution.
- \mu_{3}: Third moment of the crystal size distribution.
- C: Solution concentration expressed in mass of crystal per unit mass of solvent.

Inputs (variables no law computes):
- \Delta C: Concentration difference driving the nucleation and growth rates.
- T: Temperature.

Model-wide assumptions:
- none recorded

answer.description: This is a dynamic model of batch cooling crystallization of paracetamol from water, predicting solution concentration and crystal-size-distribution moments. It couples population and solute mass balances with power-law primary nucleation and growth driven by concentration difference, and a temperature-dependent equilibrium concentration. Parameters are estimated from metastable-zone-width experiments supplemented by concentration and particle-size measurements.
